subject: POC kickoff and rotating working sessions — proposed evening rotation for APAC coverage
messages:
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca@acme-ai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — availability for hands-on working sessions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Kai and I are excited to move into a hands-on POC with Redwood. We want to run two focused 90-minute working sessions: 1) prompt/RAG routing and function/tooling review, 2) load rehearsal and observability checks (burst + KV cache behavior). We have stakeholders across US, EU and APAC and want to avoid forcing anyone to attend at odd hours.

Suggested windows (we can commit to two dates between May 4–8):
- US-friendly: 10:00–11:30 PT / 13:00–14:30 ET
- EU-friendly: 15:00–16:30 BST / 16:00–17:30 CEST
- APAC-friendly (evening): 20:00–21:30 JST / 21:00–22:30 AEST

Can Redwood propose a rotating schedule so we alternate the session that lands in APAC evening vs US morning? Also please share an agenda and a rough runbook for the load test (we expect to push ~120–150 rps for 15m bursts).

I attached a draft agenda to this email.

Thanks — Rebecca

Attachments: acme_poc_agenda_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Kai Nakamura <kai@acme-ai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — availability for hands-on working sessions

Rebecca — great to hear, and thanks for the clear windows. We can absolutely run two 90-minute hands-on sessions and rotate which timezone gets the evening slot so the load/replay work isn't always late for the APAC team.

Proposed approach (short):
- Session A (Prompt & routing): 90 minutes — prompt review, few-shot tuning, routing rules, tool/function demos (can run in US-morning / EU-afternoon rotation)
- Session B (Load + observability): 90 minutes — synthetic load bursts, KV cache warmup, per-model latency heatmaps, tracing hooks

Initial slot proposals (I'll create calendar invites once we lock):
- Option 1 (rotate by day):
  - May 4 — Session A — 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 17:00 BST / 01:00 AEST (next day)
  - May 5 — Session B — 20:00 JST / 21:00 AEST / 04:00 BST
- Option 2 (rotate by attendee block):
  - May 6 — Session A — 13:00 PT / 16:00 ET / 21:00 BST
  - May 7 — Session B — 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET / 16:00 BST

I know those look messy across zones — my ask: can you flag which option is easier for your regional leads? I can shift the APAC-facing session earlier by up to 2 hours if that helps.

I've attached a quick redwood load-test plan and updated the agenda (v2). Karthik — can you take ownership of the routing/deployment section? Marissa — can you scope the load profile and map to hardware tiers (dedicated vs hosted) so we can make a cost/latency tradeoff recommendation during the call?

I'll follow up with a shared calendar invite and a short runbook (postmortem checklist + trace links).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: redwood-loadtest-plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), acme_poc_agenda_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: action items for Acme POC — routing + load test

Team — quick internal note (will keep Rebecca and Kai in loop):

- Karthik: please draft a 15-minute routing checklist (model variants, fallback policies, prefix caching expectations). Include any quantization/compatibility notes if we recommend smaller variants for the burst window.
- Marissa: please populate the load-test sheet with the target burst profile (120–150 rps), expected tokens per request, and the minimum GPU capacity for a 95th p99 latency SLO. Add an estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted cost for the rehearsal.

Target to have those artifacts by EOD Apr 21 PT so I can circulate them with the invite tomorrow. I'll propose Option 1 (rotate by day) as the default and let them request a swap.

Thanks — Mina
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca@acme-ai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Kai Nakamura <kai@acme-ai.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — availability for hands-on working sessions

Thanks Mina — Option 1 works best for our EU and US leads, but our APAC engineering lead has a conflicting regulatory review on May 5. Two asks: 1) can we move the APAC-friendly load rehearsal to May 4 evening (so both sessions fall within May 4–5 instead of May 4–6), and 2) can you include sub-steps in the runbook for service account scope and KMS key access (we need to run a short audit before the rehearsal)?

If you can shift Session B to May 4 at 20:00 JST / 21:00 AEST we can keep MAJOR stakeholders on both sessions. Otherwise we can do May 6 but prefer to keep it tighter.

If that works I'll approve the invites — otherwise please propose a single reschedule time and I'll confirm.

— Rebecca
